notes: ASPIRIN (batch R). Clinic product aspirin 100 mg tablets: 100 mg is not a UK strength (emc and MHRA Products list 75 mg and 300 mg); content taken from UK 75 mg plain (emc-102206) and 75 mg gastro-resistant (emc-2614) SmPCs as two formulations. Analgesic dosing (300-900 mg three to four times daily) is shown only as a detail dosing item from a UK 300 mg gastro-resistant SmPC (emc-8627, not a clinic product); NO engine rules were taken from emc-8627 except the gastro-resistant antacid rule (scoped to the gastro-resistant formulation). Its stricter items (whole third trimester and breastfeeding contraindicated; IBD caution; sulphonamide interaction) are shown as detail items only, because they belong to a higher-dose product. CONFLICTS: (a) Plain 75 mg SmPC third trimester: 4.3 says doses >100 mg/day, 4.6 says 100 mg/day and higher; gastro-resistant SmPC: >100 mg/day contraindicated, up to and including 100 mg/day only under strict obstetric monitoring. Clinic dose (100 mg) sits exactly on this boundary; rule concern names both wordings. (b) T1-T2 "should not be given unless clearly necessary" sits under the >100 mg/day heading; rule is avoid with concern scoped to >100 mg/day, plus an info rule from BUMPS (low dose can be used if recommended). (c) Breastfeeding: SmPCs short-term OK, long-term/higher doses discontinue (avoid); SPS low dose use with caution and monitor infant; 300 mg SmPC contraindicated. (d) Gout: gastro-resistant SmPC 4.3 contraindicated vs plain SmPC 4.4 warning only (formulation-scoped rules). (e) Severe cardiac insufficiency only in plain SmPC 4.3 (scoped). GROUP NOTE FOR INTEGRATOR: aspirin is NOT added to group nsaid, although the gastro-resistant SmPC says "adverse effects of NSAIDs, including acetylsalicylic acid" and lists "Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)" in 4.5. Adding it would make every nsaid-group rule from other medicines (e.g. ARB/ACE "NSAIDs incl. aspirin >3 g/day", NSAID allergy cross-reactivity) fire for low-dose aspirin; batch K already gave aspirin anti-inflammatory-dose rules separately. Integrator may decide. Interactions with medicines not in the master list (probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, digoxin, lithium, acetazolamide, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, valproate, phenytoin, metamizole, deferasirox, alcohol) are section-only. Valproate/phenytoin not mapped to group antiepileptic (would wrongly fire for carbamazepine). Antidiabetic rule uses group antidiabetic (plain SmPC "antidiabetics, e.g. sulphonylureas and insulin"). No SPS monitoring page for aspirin was found. MHRA DSU 2009 (primary prevention not licensed) used for restrictions. SPS antenatal PGD template page not used (template attachment only). Reused source ids: sps-antiplatelet-breastfeeding (C.json), sps-nsaids-asthma (A.json). Cross-direction rules from other medicines' SmPCs (warfarin, clopidogrel, sertraline, methotrexate, ibuprofen) were not added on the aspirin side; they live in those medicines' files. BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). No brand-prescribing statement found. ETORICOXIB/CELECOXIB (batch R, coxib part). Sources: etoricoxib UK SmPC emc-10616 (30/60/90/120 mg in one SmPC; clinic 90 mg); celecoxib 200 mg SmPC emc-2945 (primary) and 100 mg SmPC emc-5533 (sections 4.3 and 4.5 text identical to 200 mg; used only for the 100 mg strength line); MHRA DSU etoricoxib high blood pressure (2008) and RA/AS dose (2016); reused from batch A: mhra-dsu-nsaids-renal-2009, mhra-dsu-nsaids-pregnancy-2023, sps-bf-nsaids, sps-nsaids-asthma, sps-nsaids-monitoring; reused from other batches for cross-direction interactions: emc-2803 (warfarin SmPC names cox-2 specific NSAIDs), emc-5935 (clopidogrel SmPC names Cox-2 inhibitors), emc-987 (metformin SmPC names COX II inhibitors), emc-1070 (sertraline, NSAIDs generally), emc-1619 (spironolactone, NSAIDs generally), emc-10988 + sps-mtx-interactions (methotrexate, NSAIDs generally). No BUMPS leaflet exists for celecoxib or etoricoxib (404); SPS pain-in-pregnancy page does not mention coxibs. LEVELS: both SmPCs list pregnancy and breastfeeding in 4.3 -> contraindicated; SPS breastfeeding is less restrictive (celecoxib COX-2 inhibitor of choice with infant monitoring -> monitor; etoricoxib use with caution -> caution); kept as separate rules (CONFLICT between UK sources). Celecoxib 4.3 contraindicates women of childbearing potential without effective contraception -> condition childbearing-potential-no-contraception and attempting-to-conceive both contraindicated (4.6: contraindicated in women who can become pregnant). Etoricoxib attempting-to-conceive: not recommended (avoid). 4.3 says ACTIVE peptic ulceration/GI bleeding only; the master condition peptic-ulcer-gi-bleeding covers active or history, so the rule is contraindicated with the action text saying a past history only needs caution (4.4) - integrator may prefer an active-only condition. Etoricoxib uncontrolled hypertension (>140/90 persistently) -> NEW condition uncontrolled-hypertension (contraindicated, SmPC 4.3 + MHRA must not receive); plain hypertension -> caution with BP check within 2 weeks. NYHA II-IV heart failure mapped to both heart-failure and severe-heart-failure (contraindicated). Aspirin: both SmPCs allow low-dose aspirin with higher GI risk (caution rule); etoricoxib SmPC says aspirin above cardiovascular prophylaxis doses is not recommended - this dose-dependent avoid cannot be expressed, so it is stated in the aspirin rule action text only. group:nsaid interaction rule (etoricoxib avoid: not recommended; celecoxib avoid: non-aspirin NSAID should be avoided) - if aspirin is placed in the nsaid group the engine will also show avoid for aspirin, which overstates for low-dose aspirin. Etoricoxib + oral salbutamol: SmPC names ORAL salbutamol only (sulfotransferase); rule other salbutamol at caution with concern text saying oral; integrator may drop if the master salbutamol is inhaled only. Celecoxib CYP2D6: tricyclics and SSRIs -> dose rules (dose of individually titrated substrates may need reduction); dextromethorphan info. Celecoxib fluconazole -> dose (half dose); group cyp2c9-inhibitor caution (avoid in known CYP2C9 poor metabolisers); fluconazole added to cyp2c9-inhibitor group with celecoxib SmPC quote. Celecoxib carbamazepine (CYP2C9 inducer) info. NEW condition cyp2c9-poor-metaboliser (also defined by mefenamic part, same id). Celecoxib sulfonamide allergy: allergen group:sulfonamide, group:non-antibiotic-sulfonamide (batch M, may be empty) and sulfamethoxazole. Not in master list, section text only: ciclosporin, tacrolimus, lithium, digoxin, rifampicin, HRT, minoxidil, metoprolol, apixaban/dabigatran/rivaroxaban (covered by group:anticoagulant rule). Oral contraceptives (etoricoxib raises ethinylestradiol 37-60%) expressed as condition rule hormonal-contraception (caution). Celecoxib 4.8 frequencies: the fetched page text loses table columns; frequency columns were read from the same emc page HTML table (Very common: hypertension; Common: listed terms) and the quotes prove the terms. Celecoxib paediatric: not indicated in children -> age info rule under 18. BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). No UK source requires brand prescribing. DICLOFENAC (batch R). Five formulations kept separate: diclofenac potassium 50 mg tablets (emc-4333; clinic Cataflam and Voltaren 50 mg tablets, both mapped by the clinic monograph to this potassium SmPC - INTEGRATOR CHECK: if the clinic Voltaren 50 mg tablet is in fact diclofenac sodium gastro-resistant, the systemic content is the same but no UK gastro-resistant 50 mg SmPC was added), diclofenac sodium 100 mg prolonged-release tablets (emc-2662; clinic Voltaren Retard), diclofenac sodium suppositories (emc-7859; clinic 100 mg), and two topical gels 1.16% (emc-366) and 2.32% (emc-8775). The clinic lists a topical OINTMENT; no UK diclofenac ointment SmPC was found, the UK topical products are gels (stated in the formulation note). SCOPING: all systemic contraindications (GI ulcer/bleed, hepatic failure, renal failure, CHF NYHA II-IV, IHD, PAD, cerebrovascular disease), cautions, renal/hepatic rules and every 4.5 interaction rule are scoped to the three systemic formulations. Rules that apply to ALL forms (both gel SmPCs list them in 4.3): own-ingredient hypersensitivity, NSAID-triggered asthma/angioedema/urticaria/rhinitis (allergy + condition), third trimester contraindicated, T1-T2 should not be given unless clearly necessary, asthma caution (gel 4.4 + SPS). Gel-only rules: systemic NSAID co-use caution, breastfeeding caution (HCP advice, not on breasts), 1.16% gel under-14 contraindicated (4.3), 2.32% gel under-14 info (insufficient data), 2.32% gel any NSAID/aspirin hypersensitivity contraindicated, 2.32% gel peptic ulcer caution. Suppository-only: proctitis contraindicated (new condition proctitis). CONFLICTS: (a) Breastfeeding: tablet/suppository SmPCs should not be administered (avoid) vs SPS diclofenac is an NSAID of choice and oral, rectal and topical forms can be used (info); both kept. (b) MHRA 2023 NSAID pregnancy advice covers systemic NSAIDs only and states topical NSAIDs were not examined; the gel SmPCs themselves contraindicate the third trimester, so the T3 rule applies to all forms. AGE: prolonged-release tablets (not suitable for children) and 50/100 mg suppositories (not indicated in children) give no upper age; rules use maxYears 18 and say so in the concern. Potassium tablets: not recommended under 14 (avoid). NOT RULED (section text only, not in master list): lithium, digoxin, cardiac glycosides, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, phenytoin, colestipol/colestyramine, mifepristone, potent CYP2C9 inhibitors such as voriconazole (no master-list member is described by a UK source as a POTENT CYP2C9 inhibitor, so group cyp2c9-inhibitor was not used). Trimethoprim hyperkalaemia rule duplicated for co-trimoxazole (contains trimethoprim). Aspirin is given its own interaction and allergy entries because the aspirin entry is not in group nsaid (see aspirin note). Cross-direction rules from other medicines SmPCs (warfarin, spironolactone, lisinopril, metformin, methotrexate etc.) already exist as group:nsaid rules in those files and apply via diclofenac nsaid membership; not duplicated. Hypertension and diabetes are caution rules (significant CV risk factors: only after careful consideration, SmPC + MHRA 2013). Hyperlipidaemia and smoking have no condition id (text only). No UK source requires brand-name prescribing. NO-UK-PRODUCT: paracetamol-chlorzoxazone (no chlorzoxazone product on emc or MHRA Products; the clinic monograph emc-4195 is a paracetamol-only capsule) and orphenadrine-paracetamol (only orphenadrine hydrochloride 50 mg/5 ml oral solution for parkinsonism exists in the UK; different salt, single ingredient, not used). MEFENAMIC ACID (batch R). Clinic product: 250 mg capsules. Sources: emc SmPC (originator 250 mg capsules, emc-1598) as primary; a second UK SmPC for generic 250 mg capsules from MHRA Products (PL 4556/0045) used for the points where it differs. Reused (defined in sources/A.json, not redefined): mhra-dsu-nsaids-pregnancy-2023, mhra-dsu-nsaids-renal-2009, sps-bf-nsaids, sps-nsaids-monitoring, sps-nsaids-asthma, sps-pain-pregnancy; cross-direction quotes reuse emc-2803 (warfarin), emc-1619 (spironolactone, names mefenamic acid), emc-7611 (lisinopril), emc-987 (metformin), emc-10988 + sps-mtx-interactions (methotrexate) from other batches. CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept separate): (a) other NSAIDs incl. COX-2 inhibitors: generic SmPC lists this in section 4.3 (contraindicated rule) while the originator SmPC says 'avoid' in 4.4/4.5 (avoid rule); (b) under 12 years: originator recommends the 50 mg/5 ml suspension (info rule), generic says capsules 'Not recommended' (avoid rule); (c) breastfeeding: originator 'should not be taken by nursing mothers', generic 'should, if possible, be avoided', SPS 'should be avoided' (all avoid); (d) generic 4.3 adds intestinal ulceration (shown in contraindications section; no separate condition id). Generic 4.5 opens with 'Care should be taken ... interactions have been reported', so sulfonylurea, methotrexate, quinolone and aminoglycoside rules are caution (originator states no action for these). NOT IN MASTER LIST (section-only): lithium, cardiac glycosides, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, zidovudine, probenecid, mifepristone, heparin. No numeric renal threshold in either SmPC (renal failure -> severe-renal-impairment condition). No 4.8 frequencies ('Frequencies are not known'). No MHRA DSU specific to mefenamic acid found (gov.uk DSU search returned only monthly letters/recalls lists). NEW CONDITIONS: cabg-surgery, cyp2c9-poor-metaboliser (other NSAID files in this batch may need the same ids). BNF not accessed. brandPrescribing null (no UK source). MERGE NOTE: etoricoxib-salbutamol rule dropped at merge (SmPC names ORAL salbutamol only; the clinic salbutamol entry is inhaled); kept as section text. Aspirin is NOT in group nsaid (see aspirin note): NSAID-group allergy/interaction rules of other medicines will not fire for aspirin unless they also name aspirin. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker, see scripts/medcheck-uk/audit/R-S.md): (1) DICLOFENAC: new formulation diclofenac-gr-tab (clinic Voltaren 50 mg is diclofenac SODIUM; UK diclofenac sodium 50 mg gastro-resistant SmPC PL 00289/0739 added); all systemic rules now cover k-tab, gr-tab, mr-tab and supp (trimethoprim/co-trimoxazole rules stay on the three SmPCs that name trimethoprim); GR-only rules for lactose, children, aspirin (avoid: two or more NSAIDs including aspirin). New diclofenac:interaction:fluconazole (caution; diclofenac SmPCs: potent CYP2C9 inhibitors; celecoxib SmPC calls fluconazole a potent CYP2C9 inhibitor). Corticosteroid rules of diclofenac, aspirin, celecoxib and mefenamic acid now name prednisolone and dexamethasone (the oral corticosteroids in the master list) instead of group corticosteroid, because that group also holds nebulised budesonide and inhaled/nasal beclometasone and the SmPCs mean systemic corticosteroids. If an oral corticosteroid is added to the master list, add matching rules. (2) ASPIRIN: new formulation aspirin-analgesic (UK aspirin 300 mg tablets, PL 20395/0100; not a clinic product) so that other batches can scope dose-dependent rules with otherFormulations ["aspirin-analgesic"] and low-dose rules with ["aspirin-75-tab","aspirin-75-gr"]. Low-dose-specific aspirin rules (pregnancy, breastfeeding, methotrexate, lactose, conceive, age, anticoagulant/warfarin avoid) are now scoped to the two 75 mg formulations; analgesic-only rules added from the 300 mg SmPC 4.3 (peptic ulcer current or past, concurrent anticoagulant, GFR<15, gout, under 16, third trimester, breastfeeding all contraindicated). Aspirin hepatic rule split (moderate caution, mild monitor). (3) ETORICOXIB: aspirin rule split with otherFormulations: low-dose caution, analgesic-dose avoid. (4) CELECOXIB: cyp2c9-inhibitor group rule concern now states the CYP2C9 poor-metaboliser qualifier (group also holds fenofibrate, a mild-moderate inhibitor).
